afterlife_events.research_value: Makes the reconstruction itself an object of technical and metrological analysis rather than treating it as a neutral copy.

nineteenth_century_conditions_as_reporte: softer and more fragile soda-lime-silica glass
contemporary_reconstruction_conditions_a: transformed industrial glass compositions including borosilicate
process_mismatch_record.interpretive_guard: The Blaschka Renaissance output is an experimental reconstruction under changed technical conditions, not a literal replication of the nineteenth-century production process.
process_mismatch_record.research_payoff: The mismatch is evidence-producing: reconstruction identifies which historical gestures, materials and process parameters cannot simply be recovered by copying visible form.

digital_afterlife_schema.mandatory_distinction: A 3D gesture sequence is not a 3D scan of the historical object. Digital records must state what exactly was digitised: object geometry, internal structure, surface photography, or human movement.

upgrade_effect.before: Liège backend was already strong on acquisition chronology, count checkpoints, collection-level restoration and protected-heritage status, but had only one direct public local object identifier and no formal reconstruction/digital-afterlife event class.
after: A second distinct source-identified Liège object is now anchored: Clava multicornis, MAR-AMLG-RE11201.
The Liège chain extends from teaching object to conservation research, restoration/publication, experimental reconstruction, motion capture and digital craft-gesture surrogate.
The 2007 thesis is promoted to the top fulltext target with exact library locator data.
The schema now prevents replica/restoration/reconstruction/digitisation from collapsing into one generic afterlife field.
upgrade_effect.object_level_collection_grade: A+/S-candidate pending treatment table and 49-object identifier crosswalk
